title: Dynamic scaling of geospatial data on maps
related_application_signals: continuation lineage includes US application 16/242,615 filed 2019-01-08, now US11175157
claims priority to US provisional application 62/750,031 filed 2018-10-24

source_provenance.note: Ephemeral request-token parameters are intentionally not persisted.

classification_signals: interactive map zoom and marker rendering
publicly_described_functional_concepts: displaying a geographical map with one or more marker layers
changing marker size as map zoom or map scale changes
using low and high threshold regions to bound marker scaling behavior
determining marker-size changes using marker type, marker density, or display resolution
supporting different scale relationships for different marker types
maintaining map readability and pattern visibility without removing underlying geospatial objects

scope_model.analysis_loop: receive authorized geospatial objects -> resolve viewport, zoom, density, type, and display context -> select independently designed bounded marker-scaling policy -> render marker layers -> measure overlap/readability -> recompute on zoom or viewport change
building_patterns_relevant_to_independen: keep geographic coordinates separate from visual marker-size policy
treat zoom, marker type, density, and display resolution as independent rendering inputs
use explicit lower and upper bounds for display size
allow per-layer or per-type scaling functions instead of one global curve
preserve source objects while reducing visual clutter at extreme zoom levels
record rendering policy versions and viewport telemetry for reproducibility
keep visualization logic separate from operational or physical action logic

independent_claim_themes: map and marker-layer presentation at a first scale
changing marker size after a zoom-level change
marker type, density, or map/display resolution as scaling inputs
multiple marker types with independently configurable scaling behavior
claim_scope_signals.legal_scope_rule: Patent scope depends on controlling claims, prosecution history, legal status, and jurisdiction. This record is an engineering research abstraction only.

family_signals.territorial_status_rule: Do not infer worldwide rights or freedom to operate from this US grant or family; recheck controlling claims, prosecution history, and legal status in each relevant jurisdiction.

design_divergence_defaults: use independently designed scaling curves and threshold values
derive layout/readability objectives from product requirements rather than patent examples
keep data semantics and rendering policy in separate modules
prefer testable visual-density and accessibility metrics for tuning
avoid copying patent figures, claim wording, or exact parameter choices

mandatory_safety_boundaries: no person identification or covert tracking
